text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000043 bills 99215 well above risk-adjusted expectation, but the few charts returned support the billed levels, so the pattern cannot yet be attributed to upcoding or to a sicker panel.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"Most of this provider's 99215s fall on multi-morbid patients, as in sampled claims C0015108 and C0016405, which fits a complex panel. However, the 99215 share runs roughly two to three times the all-provider rate in every complexity band, including patients with zero conditions, and 99214 dominates the overall mix. That points to an upward shift across the board rather than only appropriate coding of sick patients. The sampled low-complexity 99215s include several single-problem visits, such as zero-condition urinary tract infection visits (C0015015, C0015687, C0015838) and isolated back pain (C0015892). These are the claims where a top-level code is hardest to justify. The documentation does not help much yet: the 5 documented 99215s all support high MDM (for example C0015692 and C0016065), and nothing suggests cloned data-review notes, but records came back for only about 1% of claims, which is too thin to judge. A reviewer should first request charts for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed in the packet, then check whether 99214 visits on low-complexity patients are similarly supported, before drawing any conclusion."}
